title: In an Emergency Situation the Operational Facilitator may compress the Root Edit timeline and withhold the announcement
content:
A.6.1.1.8.2.2.2.2.1.2.3.1 grants the emergency power: "In an Emergency Situation, as defined by the Sky Core Atlas in A.1.9.1.1 ... the Operational Facilitator may allow a Root Edit to occur more quickly than the timeline specified above. Where feasible, the Operational Facilitator should announce the decision to deploy the emergency Root Edit protocol and provide their reasoning via a public Sky Forum post ..., unless doing so would endanger Launch Agent 7 or its users."

Three features are worth separating. First, the *trigger* is external: what counts as an emergency is defined by the Atlas, not by the Facilitator or by Agent governance, which prevents the Agent from widening its own emergency conditions by amendment. Second, the *power* granted is over timing — the seven-day review and three-day poll can be shortened — rather than an explicit power to skip the token-holder vote outright. Third, the transparency duty degrades from "must" to "should ... where feasible," with an explicit carve-out for disclosure that would endanger the Agent or its users.

The secrecy carve-out is where the tension sits. The ordinary safeguard on Facilitator discretion is publicity; in exactly the situation where discretion is broadest, publicity becomes optional and the Facilitator judges its own exception. No retrospective disclosure obligation is stated once the danger has passed.

This is a common and defensible design — bounded speed for genuine crises — but its accountability rests on after-the-fact review that the Artifact does not itself schedule.
description: Emergency powers are delegated to one role using the Atlas's own definition of emergency; the duty to publish reasoning is waived where disclosure would endanger the Agent or its users.
